l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry concerns Lehi, his wife Sariah, and their four sons: Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi. The Lord warns Lehi to leave Jerusalem because he prophesies about the people’s iniquity and they seek to destroy his life. Lehi’s family travels into the wilderness, returns to Jerusalem for the record of the Jews, takes the daughters of Ishmael as wives, and later reaches the large waters. Nephi builds a ship after his brethren rebel, and the family crosses the large waters to the promised land.

l: the crossing of the large waters, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Lehi’s family crosses the large waters in the ship and reaches the promised land.

l: Nephi's record, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry
s: Nephi’s record gives the account of Lehi and his family, their travels and sufferings, the building of the ship, and their crossing into the promised land. Nephi states that he wrote the record.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi introduces himself, his family, his record, and the language and knowledge used to make it. Lehi prays for his people, receives visions of God, angels, a book, and the destruction of Jerusalem, and then prophesies to the Jews. The Jews mock and oppose Lehi, becoming angry and seeking his life. Nephi declares that the tender mercies of the Lord are over those chosen because of their faith, to make them mighty unto deliverance.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi was born of goodly parents and was taught in the learning of his father. He records his proceedings, abridges his father's record, and declares that the record is true. He will show that the tender mercies of the Lord are over those chosen because of their faith.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Lehi dwelt at Jerusalem and prayed with all his heart for his people. He saw a pillar of fire, received visions and a book, read and prophesied of Jerusalem's destruction, and was mocked and threatened by the Jews.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: God was seen by Lehi sitting upon His throne, surrounded by numberless concourses of angels singing and praising Him. Lehi praised God's works, power, goodness, and mercy.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: The things Lehi saw, heard, and read in the book manifested plainly the coming of the Messiah.

l: the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: The Jews mocked Lehi because of his testimony, became angry with him, and sought his life. They were compared with people who had cast out, stoned, and slain prophets of old.

l: the people of Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: The people of Jerusalem were warned through many prophets that they must repent or Jerusalem would be destroyed. Lehi also went among them to declare what he had seen and heard.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Jerusalem was described as facing destruction because of the abominations of its inhabitants. Many inhabitants would perish by the sword, and many would be carried captive into Babylon.

l: the book, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: A heavenly figure gave Lehi a book and commanded him to read it. The book contained testimony concerning Jerusalem's destruction, the coming of the Messiah, and the redemption of the world.

l: Nephi's record, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi makes a record in the language of his father, using the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians. He makes it with his own hand and according to his knowledge, and he abridges Lehi's record.

l: the mysteries of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi states that he had great knowledge of the goodness and the mysteries of God.

l: Lehi's visions and dreams, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Lehi saw visions and dreams that included a pillar of fire, the heavens opening, God upon His throne, angels, and a descending figure. He also saw and heard many things that he later declared to the people.

l: the destruction of Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: The destruction of Jerusalem was prophesied by many prophets and by Lehi. It would involve inhabitants perishing by the sword and being carried captive into Babylon.

l: Lehi's prayer, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Lehi prayed to the Lord with all his heart in behalf of his people. During his prayer, a pillar of fire came and dwelt upon a rock before him.

l: the coming of the Messiah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Lehi's testimony and the contents of the book manifested plainly the coming of the Messiah.

l: the redemption of the world, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Lehi's testimony and the contents of the book manifested plainly the redemption of the world.

l: the tender mercies of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi declares that the tender mercies of the Lord are over all those whom the Lord has chosen because of their faith.

l: faith, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Faith is identified as the reason the Lord's chosen people receive His tender mercies and are made mighty unto the power of deliverance.

l: the power of deliverance, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 1
s: Nephi states that the Lord's tender mercies can make those chosen because of their faith mighty even unto the power of deliverance.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The Lord warns Lehi in a dream that people seek to take his life and commands him to take his family into the wilderness. Lehi leaves his house, inheritance, gold, silver, and precious things, taking only his family, provisions, and tents, and travels to a valley near the Red Sea. The Lord speaks through Lehi and Nephi to Laman, Lemuel, and Sam, while Laman and Lemuel murmur and refuse to hearken. The Lord promises Nephi prosperity, a land of promise, and authority over his brethren if he keeps the commandments, while warning of a curse and a scourge for rebellion.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The Lord speaks to Lehi in a dream, warns him that people seek to take his life, and commands him to depart into the wilderness with his family. The Lord accepts Lehi's offering and gives Nephi promises concerning prosperity, a land of promise, authority, and the consequences of rebellion.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lehi is warned by the Lord in a dream and obeys the command to leave Jerusalem with his family. He travels in the wilderness, builds an altar, offers thanks, names the river Laman and the valley of Lemuel, and speaks with power to Laman and Lemuel.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Nephi is exceedingly young and large in stature, and he desires to know the mysteries of God. He cries unto the Lord, receives a softened heart and a manifestation by the Holy Spirit, believes his father, teaches Sam, and receives promises for his faith and obedience.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Laman is Lehi's elder son and is compared to the river Laman, which continually runs into the fountain of all righteousness. He murmurs against Lehi, refuses to hearken unto Nephi's words, and is included among those who will be cut off from the presence of the Lord if he rebels.

l: Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lemuel is Lehi's elder son and is compared to the valley of Lemuel, which is firm, steadfast, and immovable in keeping the commandments of the Lord. He murmurs against Lehi, refuses to hearken unto Nephi's words, and is included among those who will be cut off from the presence of the Lord if he rebels.

l: Lehi's family, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lehi's family consists of his mother, Sariah, and his elder brothers Laman, Lemuel, and Sam. The family departs with Lehi into the wilderness, taking provisions and tents.

l: Laman and Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Laman and Lemuel murmur against their father because he led them away from Jerusalem and their inheritance and precious things. They do not believe Jerusalem can be destroyed, refuse to hearken unto Nephi, and are confounded by Lehi when he speaks with power.

l: Lehi's seed, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lehi's seed is promised protection from the power of Laman and Lemuel's seed unless Lehi's seed rebels against the Lord. If they rebel, Laman and Lemuel's seed will be a scourge to stir them up in the ways of remembrance.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Jerusalem is the land from which Lehi and his family depart. Laman and Lemuel do not believe that Jerusalem, described as a great city, can be destroyed according to the words of the prophets.

l: the Red Sea, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The Red Sea is near the borders where Lehi travels in the wilderness. The river Laman empties into it, and the valley is near the mouth of the river.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The wilderness is where Lehi is commanded to take his family and where they travel after departing from Jerusalem. Lehi travels for three days before pitching his tent in a valley by a river of water.

l: the valley of Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The valley of Lemuel is where Lehi pitches his tent after traveling three days in the wilderness. It is near the mouth of the river Laman and is used by Lehi as an image of firmness and steadfastness in keeping the commandments.

l: the river Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The river Laman is a river of water beside which Lehi pitches his tent. It empties into the Red Sea, and Lehi names it while wishing that Laman would be like it, continually running into the fountain of all righteousness.

l: land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The land of promise is a land that the Lord has prepared for Nephi and promises to those who keep the commandments. It is described as choice above all other lands.

l: the dream, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: In a dream, the Lord speaks to Lehi, blesses him for his faithfulness, warns that people seek his life, and commands him to take his family into the wilderness.

l: Lehi's departure from Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lehi's departure occurs after the Lord commands him in a dream to take his family into the wilderness. He leaves his house, land of inheritance, gold, silver, and precious things, taking only his family, provisions, and tents.

l: the three days' journey into the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Lehi's journey takes him through the wilderness along borders near the Red Sea. After three days, he pitches his tent in a valley beside a river of water.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The commandments of the Lord are the basis for Lehi's obedience and Nephi's promised prosperity. Keeping them leads to a land of promise, while rebellion brings separation from the presence of the Lord and other stated consequences.

l: faith, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Faith is shown by Lehi, who is blessed for being faithful and declaring the commanded things, and by Nephi, who believes his father's words. Nephi is blessed because of his faith and diligent seeking of the Lord with lowliness of heart.

l: murmuring, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Murmuring is done by Laman and Lemuel against their father. They murmur because they do not understand the dealings of the God who created them and resent leaving Jerusalem and their possessions.

l: Nephi's brethren's rebellion, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: Rebellion against the Lord causes Laman and Lemuel's brethren to be cut off from the presence of the Lord. Those who rebel may receive a sore curse, and their seed may have power over Lehi's seed as a scourge.

l: the curse, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 2
s: The Lord declares that a sore curse will come upon those who rebel against him. The curse includes having no power over Lehi's seed unless Lehi's seed also rebels against the Lord.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Nephi returns to his father, who tells him that the Lord commanded Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem to obtain the records on the plates of brass from Laban. Nephi agrees to go, and he and his brothers first send Laman to request the records, then offer Laban their gold, silver, and precious things, but Laban rejects them and attempts to seize their property. After Nephi and his brothers flee into the wilderness, Laman and Lemuel mistreat Nephi and their other younger brothers until an angel of the Lord commands them to return to Jerusalem and promises that the Lord will deliver Laban into their hands. Laman and Lemuel continue to question how Laban can be delivered, since he is powerful.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Nephi returns from speaking with the Lord and agrees to go to Jerusalem to obtain the records on the plates of brass. He persuades his brothers to continue, gathers his family's gold, silver, and precious things, and insists that they fulfill the Lord's commandment. After Laman and Lemuel smite him with a rod, Nephi hears the angel promise that Laban will be delivered into their hands.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Nephi's father tells Nephi that he dreamed the Lord commanded Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem for the records on the plates of brass. He is exceedingly glad when Nephi agrees to obey, and he would perish if he remained in Jerusalem after being commanded to flee.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: The Lord commands Nephi and his brothers to obtain the records on the plates of brass from Laban. He favors Nephi for not murmuring, prepares a way for His commandments to be accomplished, and promises through an angel to deliver Laban into their hands.

l: Nephi's brothers, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Nephi's brothers initially murmur about returning to Jerusalem and later attempt to obtain the records from Laban with gold, silver, and precious things. After losing their property and fleeing into the wilderness, they become angry, and some of them smite Nephi and their other younger brothers with a rod.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Laman is chosen by lot to enter Laban's house and request the records, but Laban rejects him, calls him a robber, and threatens to slay him. Laman later becomes angry with Nephi and smites him with a rod, then questions how the Lord could deliver Laban into their hands.

l: Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Lemuel hearkens to Laman's words, joins him in speaking hard words to their younger brothers, and smites them with a rod. After the angel departs, Lemuel continues to murmur with Laman about the possibility of overcoming Laban.

l: Laban, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Laban possesses the records on the plates of brass and refuses Laman's request for them. He rejects Nephi and his brothers when they offer their property, lusts after their wealth, sends servants to slay them, and is promised to be delivered into their hands.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: Jerusalem is the land to which Nephi and his brothers return to obtain the records. Nephi's father says Jerusalem must be destroyed because its people rejected the words of the prophets.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: The wilderness is where Nephi's father has taken his family after being commanded to flee Jerusalem. Nephi and his brothers travel through it, flee into it after losing their property, and hide in the cavity of a rock.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: The records on the plates of brass contain the genealogy of Nephi's father and the words spoken by the holy prophets through the Spirit and power of God. Nephi's father commands his sons to obtain them so they can preserve their language and the prophets' words for their children.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: The commandments of the Lord require Nephi and his brothers to return to Jerusalem and obtain the records on the plates of brass. Nephi teaches that the Lord gives no commandment without preparing a way for people to accomplish it, and he urges his brothers to remain faithful in keeping the commandments.

l: the angel of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 3
s: The angel of the Lord appears while Laman and Lemuel are smiting Nephi and asks why they do so. The angel says the Lord has chosen Nephi to rule over them because of their iniquities and promises that the Lord will deliver Laban into their hands, then departs.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi persuades his brethren to return to Jerusalem, enters the city by night, and finds Laban drunk outside his house. Led by the Spirit and commanded by the Lord, Nephi kills Laban and takes the plates of brass, which contain the law needed for his people to keep the commandments of the Lord. Nephi disguises himself in Laban’s garments and persuades Zoram to retrieve the plates and leave Jerusalem with him and his brethren. Zoram swears an oath to remain with them, and they all depart into the wilderness to Nephi’s father.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi urges his brethren to trust in the Lord and return to Jerusalem. He enters the city, kills Laban at the Spirit’s command, takes Laban’s garments and sword, obtains the plates of brass with Zoram’s help, and returns to his brethren before departing into the wilderness.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Laman initially follows Nephi to Jerusalem but later flees when he sees Nephi dressed as Laban, believing that Laban has killed Nephi and is seeking their lives. He stops fleeing when Nephi calls after him.

l: Laban, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Laban is found drunk outside his house in Jerusalem. The Spirit says that the Lord has delivered him into Nephi’s hands, and Nephi kills him with his own sword because he had sought Nephi’s life, rejected the Lord’s commandments, and taken Nephi’s family’s property.

l: Zoram, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Zoram is Laban’s servant and holds the keys to Laban’s treasury. Believing Nephi is Laban, he follows him to the plates of brass, then agrees to go into the wilderness and swears to remain with Nephi and his brethren.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: The Lord is described as mightier than all the earth and able to deliver Nephi and his brethren. He delivers Laban into Nephi’s hands, commands Nephi’s actions through the Spirit, and has taught that Nephi’s seed will prosper if they keep His commandments.

l: the Spirit and power of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: The Spirit leads Nephi into Jerusalem without his knowing beforehand what he should do. It commands Nephi to kill Laban, reminding him that the Lord has delivered Laban into his hands and that it is better for one man to perish than for a nation to dwindle in unbelief.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi and his brethren intend to return to their father in the wilderness with the plates of brass and Zoram. Zoram is promised a place with them if he goes down in the wilderness to Nephi’s father.

l: Nephi's brothers, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi’s brethren are initially angry and continue to murmur, but they follow him to Jerusalem. Laman, Lemuel, and Sam flee when they mistake Nephi for Laban, then return after Nephi calls to them and depart with him into the wilderness.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi and his brethren hide outside the walls of Jerusalem at night. Nephi enters the city to reach Laban’s house and later leaves it with Zoram and the plates of brass.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi and his brethren leave Jerusalem and journey into the wilderness with Zoram and the plates of brass. Their father is in the wilderness, where they intend to reunite with him.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: The plates of brass contain the engravings of the law of Moses. Nephi understands that the Lord delivered Laban into his hands so he could obtain the plates, and he carries them out of Jerusalem to his brethren.

l: the law of Moses, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi thinks that his people cannot keep the commandments of the Lord according to the law of Moses unless they have the law. He knows that the law is engraved on the plates of brass.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi urges his brethren to be faithful and diligent in keeping the commandments of the Lord. The text teaches that Nephi’s seed will prosper in the land of promise if they keep them.

l: Laban's sword, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Laban’s sword has a hilt of pure gold, fine workmanship, and a blade of precious steel. Nephi draws it from its sheath and uses it to kill Laban, then wears it while impersonating Laban.

l: Nephi's flight into the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Nephi’s flight into the wilderness is intended to take his brethren, the plates of brass, and Zoram away from Jerusalem. Nephi and his brethren fear that the Jews might learn of their flight, pursue them, and destroy them.

l: Laban's death, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Laban’s death occurs after the Spirit commands Nephi to slay him. Nephi takes Laban by the hair and cuts off his head with Laban’s own sword so that he can obtain the plates of brass.

l: oath of Zoram, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 4
s: Zoram makes an oath to go into the wilderness with Nephi and his brethren and to remain with them from that time forth. After he makes the oath, their fears concerning him cease.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi’s family returns to the wilderness with the plates of brass, and Lehi and Sariah rejoice after learning that the Lord protected Nephi and his brothers. Lehi searches the plates, learns of his genealogy and their contents, and prophesies concerning his seed and the records. The Lord commands Nephi and his brothers to bring Ishmael and his family from Jerusalem, and after a rebellion they return safely. Lehi then recounts a dream in which a tree, its fruit, a river, an iron rod, a path, darkness, and a great building represent dangers and choices affecting his family and their seed.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi rejoices when his sons return and searches the plates of brass. He learns their contents, discovers his genealogy, prophesies concerning his seed, and recounts a dream in which he fears for Laman and Lemuel.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Nephi returns with his brothers to Jerusalem to bring Ishmael and his family into the wilderness. He speaks to Laman and Lemuel during their rebellion, prays for deliverance, and records Lehi’s dream.

l: Sariah, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Sariah rejoices when her sons return and is comforted. She testifies that the Lord commanded Lehi to flee, protected her sons, and gave them power to obtain the records.

l: Laman, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Laman rebels with Lemuel and others while traveling with Ishmael’s family and desires to return to Jerusalem. In Lehi’s dream, he does not partake of the fruit, and Lehi fears that he may be cast off from the Lord’s presence.

l: Lemuel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lemuel rebels with Laman and others and seeks to return to Jerusalem. In Lehi’s dream, he does not partake of the fruit, and Lehi fears for him.

l: Sam, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Sam returns with Nephi and their brothers to bring Ishmael’s family into the wilderness. He is among those whom Lehi sees near the river and who partake of the fruit.

l: Ishmael, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Ishmael gains favor with Nephi and takes his household into the wilderness. During the journey, he joins those who oppose the rebellion against Nephi.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: The Lord protects Nephi and his brothers, enables them to obtain the records, and commands Lehi’s sons to bring Ishmael and his family into the wilderness. He answers Nephi’s prayer by loosing his bands and leads Lehi’s family toward the land of promise.

l: Lehi's family, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi’s family rejoices and offers sacrifice after Nephi and his brothers return with the records. They travel in the wilderness with Ishmael’s family and gather seeds of every kind.

l: Ishmael's family, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Ishmael’s family travels from Jerusalem into the wilderness with Nephi and his brothers. Some members rebel during the journey, while others plead for Nephi’s life and help soften the rebels’ hearts.

l: the seed of Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi prophesies that the plates of brass will go forth to the nations, kindreds, tongues, and people who are of his seed. He also sees that Nephi and Sam, and many of their seed, will be saved.

l: the wilderness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi’s family travels through the wilderness toward the land of promise. Lehi’s dream includes a dark and dreary wilderness and a dark and dreary waste.

l: Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Nephi and his brothers return to Jerusalem to obtain the records and later to bring Ishmael and his family into the wilderness. Nephi warns that those who return to Jerusalem will perish with its inhabitants.

l: land of promise, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi has obtained a land of promise and rejoices in it. Nephi teaches that faithfulness will allow them to obtain it.

l: the plates of brass, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: The plates of brass contain the five books of Moses, a record of the Jews, the prophecies of holy prophets including Jeremiah, and Lehi’s genealogy. Lehi prophesies that they will go forth to Lehi’s seed and never perish or be dimmed by time.

l: the commandments of the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi’s family preserves the commandments of the Lord through the plates of brass. Lehi exhorts Laman and Lemuel to keep the commandments after recounting his dream.

l: the destruction of Jerusalem, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Nephi teaches that the word of the Lord concerning the destruction of Jerusalem will be fulfilled. He says the Spirit of the Lord will soon cease to strive with the people because they rejected the prophets and sought Lehi’s life.

l: Lehi's dream, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Lehi’s dream shows a dark wilderness, a tree with desirable fruit, a river of water, an iron rod, a strait and narrow path, a mist of darkness, and a great and spacious building. It causes Lehi to rejoice for Nephi and Sam and to fear for Laman and Lemuel.

l: the river of water, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, the river of water runs near the tree and has a head where Sariah, Sam, and Nephi stand. Many are drowned in its depths, and others are lost while wandering in strange roads.

l: the tree of life, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, the tree stands in a large and spacious field and bears fruit desirable to make one happy. Lehi partakes of its fruit and desires his family to partake also.

l: the fruit of the tree, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: The fruit of the tree is sweet, white, and desirable above all other fruit. Those who partake of it experience great joy, though some become ashamed because of people mocking them.

l: the rod of iron, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, the rod of iron extends along the bank of the river and leads to the tree. Those who cling to it press through the mist of darkness and reach the tree to partake of its fruit.

l: the strait and narrow path, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, the strait and narrow path leads to the tree and passes by the head of the fountain toward a large and spacious field. Some who begin on the path lose their way when the mist of darkness arises.

l: the great and spacious building, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, the great and spacious building stands high above the earth across the river and is filled with finely dressed people. Its occupants mock those who partake of the fruit, causing some to become ashamed and fall away.

l: the mist of darkness, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: In Lehi’s dream, an exceedingly great mist of darkness causes people on the path to lose their way and become lost. Others pass through it while clinging to the rod of iron.

l: return to Jerusalem for the records, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 5 .. Chapter 8
s: Nephi and his brothers return to Jerusalem to obtain the record of the Jews. They successfully bring the plates of brass back to Lehi’s family, who search them and find them desirable and of great worth.

l: The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Nephi records Lehi’s teachings about the Jews, the Messiah, the gospel, the Gentiles, and the scattering and gathering of the house of Israel. Nephi receives a vision in which an angel shows him the tree of life, the virgin and the Son of God, the Messiah’s baptism, ministry, crucifixion, resurrection, and the work of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. He also sees the land of promise, the destruction of many cities, the appearance of the Lamb of God, and the ministry of twelve disciples among his seed. The angel explains that the tree of life represents the love of God, the rod of iron represents the word of God, the mists of darkness represent the temptations of the devil, and the large and spacious building represents vain imaginations and pride.

l: Nephi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Nephi records his father’s teachings and desires to know the things his father saw. He receives a vision by the power of the Holy Ghost, sees the ministry and suffering of the Lamb of God, and is shown the future of his seed and the seed of his brethren.

l: Lehi, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: Lehi teaches his sons about the Jews, the Messiah, the gospel, the Gentiles, and the scattering and gathering of the house of Israel. He had seen the tree, the rod of iron, the fountain, the mists of darkness, and the large and spacious building in a vision.

l: the Lord, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Lord commands Nephi to make plates for an account of the ministry of his people and prepares a way to accomplish all his works. He raises up a Messiah among the Jews and has all power unto the fulfilling of his words.

l: the Holy One of Israel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: He is identified as the Messiah, the Savior of the world, the Redeemer, the Lamb of God, and the Son of God. He is baptized, ministers among the people, is judged and crucified, rises from the dead, and shows himself to the people.

l: the Spirit and power of God, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Holy Ghost is the gift of God to those who diligently seek him and gives Nephi authority to speak. It comes upon the Messiah in the form of a dove, bears record of him, and falls upon twelve others who are chosen to minister to Nephi’s seed.

l: the angel, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: An angel shows Nephi the virgin, the Son of God, the Messiah’s ministry and suffering, the future of Nephi’s seed, and the meanings of the symbols from Lehi’s vision. The angel explains the fountain, mists of darkness, large and spacious building, and the twelve ministers.

l: the Jews, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Jews are taught to be destroyed and carried captive into Babylon, then returned to the land of their inheritance. They dwindle in unbelief, slay the Messiah, and are later described in relation to the scattering and gathering of the house of Israel.

l: the Gentiles, The First Book of Nephi, His Reign and Ministry, Chapter 9 .. Chapter 12
s: The Gentiles receive the fulness of the Gospel, after which the natural branches of the olive-tree, or remnants of the house of Israel, are grafted in and come to the knowledge of the true Messiah.
